summary: Duplicate downstream tool executions when SDK rotates per-request id mid-stream
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that during long-running streaming sessions, when the client-side SDK rotates a per-request id value mid-stream (they implemented a per-request nonce rotation to try to avoid stale-ack replays), downstream tool invocations are executed twice. The duplicates are visible in AtlasChat's backend logs and cause side effects (duplicate emails/jobs).

Impact:
- Multiple customers experienced duplicate third-party webhook calls and duplicate job enqueues leading to billing spikes and user-visible duplicate actions.
- Reported against a handful of high-throughput chat sessions for AtlasChat (Dedicated cluster, us-east region).
- Severity: customer is blocking rollback of a new feature until duplication root cause is understood.

Environment:
- Customer: AtlasChat Inc. (dedicated)
- SDKs in use: python 1.4.1 (async streaming), go 0.9.x client used in parallel workers
- Deployment: Dedicated pool rtx-a100 (us-east), API gateway w/managed edge proxy in front
- Models: gptj-redwood-13b (primary), open-compat-3.7 (fallback)

Steps to reproduce (from customer):
1) Start an async streaming session using Python SDK with per-request nonce header X-Req-Id that the customer rotates every ~30s.
2) Server generates a tool call (webhook POST to their system) triggered by a function_call in the streaming transcript.
3) Mid-stream, the client rotates X-Req-Id and continues the stream without reconnecting.
4) Server appears to treat the later frames as a new request and replays the tool invocation, resulting in two webhook posts for a single logical tool call.

Expected behavior:
- Rotating a per-request client nonce mid-stream should not cause duplicated tool invocations. The server should use an idempotency scope tied to the session or to a stable tool-call identifier emitted earlier in the stream.

Actual behavior:
- A second downstream tool invocation is executed after the header rotation point. The second invocation has a different request id in logs but the same function_call payload.

Relevant logs (anonymized excerpts from customer):
- at 2026-03-10T16:22:31Z Serving: func_call id=fc_1 request_id=req-abc123 X-Req-Id=nonce-793
- at 2026-03-10T16:22:59Z Edge: header X-Req-Id rewritten -> nonce-793-rotated
- at 2026-03-10T16:23:01Z Serving: func_call id=fc_1 request_id=req-def456 X-Req-Id=nonce-793-rotated
- atlas backend: webhook POST /enqueue job_id=job-998 duplicate_of=job-997

Additional notes from customer:
- They call out they are using a per-request-id rotation as a mitigation for a separate session-staleness problem and did not expect that to change idempotency semantics.
- When they pin X-Req-Id for the life of the streaming session duplicates disappear.
investigation_notes:
Initial triage (2026-03-11):
- Replicated with internal harness using Python SDK v1.4.1: rotating header mid-stream triggers a second tool invocation.
- Hypothesis: idempotency scope is currently derived from a combination of (session_token, X-Req-Id) in the API gateway layer. When X-Req-Id changes, the gateway normalizes headers and the request is routed to a different backend connection resulting in re-evaluation and re-emission of the pending function_call.
- Edge proxy (managed) rewrite observed: long nonces that included a colon were truncated; some LB rules added suffix "-rotated" to preserve uniqueness. This causes the edge to emit a distinct header value to downstream which then increments the request fingerprint.
- Serving runtime: function_call dedup currently keyed by (session_id, request_fingerprint). request_fingerprint built from headers + frame counter. Rotating the header changes fingerprint -> treated as new invocation.
- Also confirmed that if the SDK instead sends a stable per-session id in the additional header X-Session-Id and rotates X-Req-Id, server still deduplicates by X-Session-Id if present. This suggests acceptability of a per-session stable id fallback.

Supporting artifacts:
- Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C_SUPPORT/p1620xxxxx (internal)
- Related PR with kernel change (investigation): https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/874
- Repro harness: https://git.company.internal/atlaschat/repro-stream-rotate
resolution:
Workaround provided 2026-03-12:
- Instructed AtlasChat to set X-Session-Id (stable for session) in addition to their rotating X-Req-Id. This prevents duplication immediately.
- Customer implemented the workaround and confirmed no further duplicates in their next 24h run.

Planned fixes and rollout:
- Edge config: infra will disable the header suffix rewrite for X-Req-Id on dedicated pools (scheduled 2026-03-14 maintenance window).
- SDK change: patch queued to add convenience option `session_id` for streaming clients and to document that per-request id rotation can change idempotency unless a stable session id is supplied. Target SDK release: python 1.4.2 (2026-03-18), go 0.9.3 (2026-03-18).
- Server change: design doc for server-assigned tool_call_id submitted and under review (PR link in related_github_prs). Implementation planned Q2 2026.

Follow-ups:
- Add telemetry to detect header-value changes mid-stream and emit counts to SLO dashboard.
- Update public docs with recommended patterns for streaming idempotency.
